days.title: Northern Peaks and the Village
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Vindbelgjarfjall
stops.detail: The peaks of Vindbelgjarfjall in the north of the lake and the steaming Námafjall in the northeast offer a beautiful view over the lake.

stops.name: Reykjahlíð
stops.detail: The church of the village Reykjahlíð on the shore of the lake, and with it the inhabitants of the village at that time, was just barely spared by a lava flow in the 18th century.

stops.name: Jarðböð
stops.detail: To compensate, parts of the proceeds from the privatization were used for the expansion of the "Jarðböð" (German Earth Baths) thermal bath to create new jobs.

days.title: Volcanic Formations and Caves
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Hverfjall
stops.detail: Additionally, the volcanic explosion crater of Hverfjall (or Hverfell) is located not far from the lake, and it can also be climbed.

stops.name: Dimmuborgir
stops.detail: Below Hverfjall lies the area Dimmuborgir (German "dark castles"), charming tuff stone formations that are however threatened in their existence.

stops.name: Grjótagjá
stops.detail: The bathing caves Grjótagjá and Stóragjá can be used for bathing again to a limited extent due to the temperatures having dropped slightly in the meantime.

days.title: Southern Craters and Ridges
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Skútustaðir
stops.detail: In the lake itself, on islands and peninsulas, you can see the pseudocraters of Skútustaðir, which did not eject volcanic material themselves but were formed by the explosive encounter of lava and water.

stops.name: Lúdentsborgir
stops.detail: In the vicinity of the lake, one also finds the Lúdentsborgir crater row, table mountains and shield volcanoes.
